reply.answer_text: A Scottish member taking drawdown income is subject to **Scottish income tax rates on the pension income via PAYE with an S-code**. Relief at source (RAS) still adds 20% to ongoing contributions. If the member is a Scottish intermediate-rate (21%), higher-rate (42%), advanced-rate (45%) or top-rate (48%) taxpayer, they claim the extra relief above 20% via HMRC. Starter-rate (19%) members keep the full 20% — HMRC does not claw it back.
